To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) current methods in the AISC Seismic Commentary for determining design loads for vertical boundary elements in SPSWs do not necessarily lead VBEs to remain essentially elastic under the forces generated from fully yielded web plates; (2) a new procedure is developed that uses a fundamental collapse mechanism to determine design loads for VBEs; and (3) this new procedure is practical for design and leads to VBEs with essentially elastic behavior under fully yielded web plates.

(1) the current capacity design procedure provided by the AISC Seismic Design Provisions is not adequate for ensuring essentially elastic behavior of VBEs of steel plate shear walls and that (2) a new capacity design procedure is proposed that is more reliable and is practical to apply in design

(a) the commentary procedures for determining capacity design forces for VBEs do not always lead to VBE designs that meet the capacity design objective, and (b) a new procedure for determining capacity design VBE loads for SPSWs is presented that is practical for use in the design of VBEs
